standard.title: Specialist and technical vocabulary
standard.description: Investigate the role of vocabulary in building specialist and technical knowledge, including terms that have both everyday and technical meanings
standard.prior_knowledge: Students can identify how authors use figurative and emotive vocabulary (AC9E6LA08). They have not yet investigated how specialist and technical vocabulary functions to build disciplinary knowledge, or examined the particular challenge of terms that carry both everyday and technical meanings.
standard.progression_endpoint: Students investigate how vocabulary builds specialist knowledge, including terms with everyday and technical meanings.

nodes.label: Specialist and technical vocabulary
nodes.progression_checkpoint: Students can identify specialist and technical vocabulary in a text and explain what role it plays in building knowledge in that field
nodes.minimum_width: In a given specialist or technical text, identify at least three technical terms and explain why precise vocabulary is needed in this field
nodes.typical_width: Identify technical vocabulary across two different subject areas and discuss how specialist vocabulary enables precision and shared understanding within a discipline — what would be lost if everyday language were used instead?
wider: Investigate high utility academic vocabulary — words like 'factor', 'hypothesise', 'issue' and 'critique' — that appear across multiple disciplines and carry specific meanings in each
Examine vocabulary used to discuss a specific topic (e.g. poetic devices) and explore how the technical terms enable more precise discussion than everyday language would allow

response_modes.reason: Students commonly treat technical vocabulary as jargon to memorise rather than as a knowledge-building tool. Seeing specialist vocabulary functioning across different disciplines — and understanding that precision enables shared understanding — shifts the conception from rote learning to purposeful investigation.

success_criteria: Identifies specialist or technical vocabulary in a given text
Explains why precise vocabulary is needed in that field

nodes.label: Terms with everyday and technical meanings
nodes.progression_checkpoint: Students can identify terms that carry both everyday and technical meanings and explain how context determines which meaning applies
nodes.minimum_width: Given a term with both everyday and technical meanings (e.g. 'power', 'force', 'argument'), explain the everyday meaning and at least one technical meaning; give a sentence example of each
nodes.typical_width: Investigate several terms with dual everyday/technical meanings across different disciplines; explain how context signals which meaning applies and discuss what confusion can arise when the distinction is not made
wider: Examine how the same term ('critique', 'analyse', 'evaluate') carries different technical meanings in English compared to other subjects, and discuss how students learn to shift between them
Investigate how misunderstanding a technical term as its everyday counterpart leads to disciplinary misunderstanding — trace a specific example of this in a student-facing text

response_modes.reason: The everyday/technical distinction is a persistent source of confusion across subjects — students apply everyday meanings to technical terms across all their learning. Seeing this pattern across multiple disciplines (not just English) helps students develop a generalised awareness of the distinction rather than just learning specific word definitions.

nodes.width_opportunity_reason: This node has genuine cross-curricular richness — the everyday/technical distinction operates in Science, Maths, History and English simultaneously. Advancing students who investigate this across subjects build a metacognitive awareness of how disciplinary knowledge is encoded in vocabulary.
success_criteria: Identifies at least one term with both everyday and technical meanings
Explains both meanings and gives an example of each in context
